title: The Late Will
premise: When the coffin of Harlan Voss, founder of the fog-bound town of Meridian Falls, is exhumed for a land dispute and found empty, true-crime podcaster Sebastian Eriksen arrives to cover the story—only to discover the empty grave connects to a forty-year-old disappearance they've chased for years: the vanished witness, June Calloway. As Sebastian digs through Voss's empire of philanthropy and fear, they learn the town's founding families buried more than a body—they buried a living woman who has been hiding in plain sight ever since. The statute of limitations on the original crime expires in thirty days, forcing Sebastian to find June before Voss's heirs can silence her permanently. In the end, Sebastian finds June alive but transformed, chooses exposure over safety, and broadcasts the truth even as it costs them their anonymity and nearly their life.
about_author: Ansel Galloway is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering municipal corruption in the Pacific Northwest before turning to fiction. They live off-grid with two dogs and an unhealthy interest in probate law.

chapters.title: The Weight of Dirt
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Sebastian, arriving in Meridian Falls to record the exhumation of town founder Harlan Voss. They establish their rule: never take a case they can't close. The crowd's grief feels rehearsed. Emotional beat: professional detachment masking a private obsession with the town's oldest unsolved case.

chapters.title: Empty
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV as the coffin is opened before witnesses: no remains, only river stones and a rotted wool coat. The coroner pales; the Voss heirs exchange glances. Sebastian records everything. Beat: cold shock hardening into hunger—the story just became personal.

chapters.title: Thirty Days
chapters.summary: Sebastian learns the exhumation was triggered by a land claim whose legal window closes when the statute on the 1984 Calloway disappearance expires. Their producer warns them off; Sebastian signs a lease anyway. Beat: quiet commitment, the first door closing behind them.

chapters.title: The Founder's Face
chapters.summary: POV shifts briefly to elderly archivist Mabel Dunn, who catalogs Voss memorabilia and notices his portrait has been moved. She remembers a girl named June who worked the Voss estate. Beat: nostalgia curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Interviews with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sebastian interviews the Voss heirs: charming Whitaker, brittle Camille, and silent youngest son Alder. Each gives a polished account of 1984 that contradicts the others by inches. Beat: the pleasure of the hunt, first cracks in the family armor.

chapters.title: River Stones
chapters.summary: Sebastian traces the stones in the coffin to a quarry closed in 1985—the same year the Voss estate expanded its grounds. Someone refilled that coffin deliberately, recently. Beat: unease; this wasn't decay, it was design.

chapters.title: What Mabel Kept
chapters.summary: Mabel gives Sebastian a box of unfiled clippings, including one photo of June Calloway at a Voss gala—standing beside a young woman whose face is scratched out. Beat: tenderness toward the dead girl, first real fear.

chapters.title: The Podcast Problem
chapters.summary: Sebastian's episode goes viral; tourists flood the town. The mayor asks them, sweetly, to leave. A brick comes through the rental's window that night. Beat: visibility as threat—the invisible podcaster becomes a target.

chapters.title: Alder's Silence
chapters.summary: Alder Voss, drunk, tells Sebastian his father didn't kill anyone—but his father knew who did, and paid for it every year on the same date. He won't say more. Beat: pity and frustration; the heir is both cage and key.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: In county records Sebastian finds annual cash withdrawals by Harlan Voss, every June 12th from 1985 until his death—payments to someone. Beat: electric discovery, the case acquiring a spine.

chapters.title: Camille's Version
chapters.summary: Camille Voss invites Sebastian for tea and delivers a counter-narrative: June Calloway wasn't a victim, she was blackmailing her father. She shows Sebastian a threatening letter signed 'J.C.' Beat: vertigo—sympathy for June begins to wobble.

chapters.title: Scratched Out
chapters.summary: Sebastian enhances the gala photo; the scratched-out woman wears a nurse's uniform from St. Ambrose Sanatorium, long demolished. Beat: grim determination, following paper trails into ash.

chapters.title: The Man Who Watches
chapters.summary: Sebastian notices a figure at the edge of their recordings across three episodes—same coat, same gait. They set a trap with a decoy recorder. Beat: paranoia sharpening into method.

chapters.title: Trap
chapters.summary: The decoy works: the watcher is Deputy Cora Reyes, who confesses her own father investigated the Calloway case and died believing June lived. She's been protecting something—a file her father hid. Beat: alliance formed in mutual grief.

chapters.title: Reyes File
chapters.summary: Cora's father's file names a suspect: estate caretaker Emil Brandt, who confessed, recanted, and hanged himself in 1986. But the file also contains a hospital admission slip dated after his death—for J. Calloway. Beat: hope rekindled; the dead witness may breathe.

chapters.title: Whitaker Pushes Back
chapters.summary: Whitaker Voss offers Sebastian a producing deal—money, access, a book—to steer the story toward 'closure' with Brandt as sole killer. Sebastian declines. That night their car brakes fail. Beat: temptation refused, danger made physical.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Date
chapters.summary: June 12th arrives. Sebastian stakes out the cemetery and watches a hooded figure lay lilies on the empty grave. They give chase through fog and lose them—but find a dropped glove, monogrammed 'JC.' Beat: breathless midpoint; the witness is alive and mourning her own grave.

chapters.title: Reading the Town
chapters.summary: Sebastian canvasses old-timers with the enhanced photo. A diner cook recognizes the nurse: 'That's Ruthie. Works the pharmacy. Been here forever.' Beat: the uncanny thrill of the hidden-in-plain-sight reveal approaching.

chapters.title: Ruthie
chapters.summary: Sebastian visits the pharmacy and meets Ruth Callahan—older, calm, unmistakably the scratched-out woman. Ruth serves them politely and says nothing. Sebastian leaves a business card. Beat: charged stillness; two hunters recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Ruth's POV
chapters.summary: Shift to Ruth: she has been June Calloway for forty years, protected by Harlan Voss himself, who helped her disappear because what she witnessed would have destroyed not him but the town's other founders. Beat: weary vigilance, decades of performed ordinariness cracking.

chapters.title: What June Saw
chapters.summary: Ruth/June tells Sebastian part of it: in 1984 she saw not a murder but a cover-up—Harlan's brother dying of exposure in the mines, and the founders burying the cause. Emil Brandt took the fall willingly. Beat: moral complexity; the villain is a system, not a man.

chapters.title: The Missing Half
chapters.summary: June refuses to name who ordered the cover-up without proof: her testimony alone dies with the statute. The proof is in Harlan's private papers, now split among the three heirs. Beat: frustration and resolve; truth needs corroboration.

chapters.title: Dividing the Dead Man's Paper
chapters.summary: Sebastian plays the heirs against each other, leaking hints of the ledger to each. Whitaker panics; Camille lawyers up; Alder calls Sebastian at 3 a.m., ready to talk. Beat: Machiavellian momentum, power beginning to corrupt everyone it touches.

chapters.title: Alder's Bargain
chapters.summary: Alder trades his third of the papers for Sebastian's promise to shield him from prosecution. Inside: correspondence showing Harlan funded June's exile—and a second ledger in another hand. Beat: uneasy complicity; Sebastian breaks their own clean-hands rule.

chapters.title: The Second Hand
chapters.summary: Forensic comparison suggests the second ledger belongs to the current mayor, who was Harlan's protégé in 1984. The cover-up never ended; it changed management. Beat: dawning horror—the rot is present tense.

chapters.title: Brick and Fire
chapters.summary: Someone burns the archive room at the historical society. Mabel is hospitalized with smoke inhalation. Sebastian realizes their published episode tipped off the mayor. Beat: guilt, rage, the cost of visibility made flesh.

chapters.title: Mabel's Testimony
chapters.summary: From her hospital bed, Mabel identifies the arsonist's truck—mayor's office fleet. She also reveals she's known who Ruth was for years and kept silent out of loyalty. Beat: grief braided with betrayal; even protectors are prisoners of the town.

chapters.title: Cora Crosses Lines
chapters.summary: Deputy Reyes pulls the fleet logs illegally to help Sebastian. The mayor suspends her. Cora, undeterred, gives Sebastian her father's last letter—which names the mine shaft where evidence was buried. Beat: loyalty vs. law; allies spending themselves like currency.

chapters.title: The Shaft
chapters.summary: Sebastian and Cora enter the sealed mine and find a strongbox: mine inspection reports proving the fatal collapse was foreseen and covered up, plus Harlan's full confession, held over him by whoever kept the second ledger. Beat: triumph shadowed by claustrophobic dread.

chapters.title: Ambush
chapters.summary: Leaving the mine, they're run off the road. The strongbox is stolen; Cora is injured shielding it. Sebastian escapes with photographs taken minutes before. Beat: brutal loss; the price of evidence is blood.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Five days remain. The mayor announces a memorial 'healing ceremony' at the cemetery—an obvious stage-managed ending. Sebastian understands: the town will bury the truth with honors. Beat: cornered urgency, the clock audible in every scene.

chapters.title: Turning Ruth
chapters.summary: Sebastian confronts Ruth with the photographed confession: Harlan protected her because she was the only witness he trusted—and the mayor's faction wants her dead now that the grave is open. Ruth agrees to testify, but only publicly, on the record. Beat: courage kindled in the quietest character.

chapters.title: Whitaker's Choice
chapters.summary: Sebastian shows Whitaker the second ledger's implications: his family's fortune rests on the cover-up continuing. Torn between legacy and conscience, he returns the stolen strongbox anonymously. Beat: redemption flickering in a weak man.

chapters.title: The Mayor's Counterstrike
chapters.summary: The mayor leaks a fabricated story branding Sebastian a fraud who staged the empty coffin. Sponsors drop the podcast; Sebastian's reputation—their identity itself—is dismantled overnight. Beat: darkest hour; the investigator becomes the accused.

chapters.title: Alone With It
chapters.summary: Sebastian, ruined and tempted to flee, rereads their own rule: never take a case you can't close. They realize invisibility was always a lie they told themselves. They call Ruth: we go tomorrow, at the ceremony. Beat: stillness before the storm; identity reclaimed through choice.

chapters.title: The Healing Ceremony
chapters.summary: At the graveside, before cameras and the whole town, the mayor eulogizes Harlan Voss. Sebastian walks forward and interrupts—not with accusation, but with a microphone and a live feed. Beat: heart-pounding public climax, all eyes converging.

chapters.title: June Speaks
chapters.summary: Ruth removes her pharmacy badge and says her name: June Calloway, witness. She testifies to the mine cover-up as Sebastian streams the photographed confession. The crowd turns; the mayor's face collapses. Beat: cathartic eruption—forty years of silence broken in ten minutes.

chapters.title: Arrests and Aftermath
chapters.summary: State police, tipped by Cora's restored badge, arrest the mayor mid-ceremony. Whitaker cooperates fully; Camille flees; Alder weeps with relief. The statute question dissolves—new charges supersede the old ones. Beat: justice arriving messy but real.

chapters.title: Closing the Case
chapters.summary: Sebastian releases the final episode: not the coldest case closed, but a living town forced to warm itself. Downloads explode; offers pour in. Sebastian turns down a network deal, keeping ownership of their own voice. Beat: bittersweet vindication; power declined is power kept.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Epilogue, months later: Sebastian stays in Meridian Falls, renting Mabel's old apartment above the archive. June tends a garden over the empty grave, planting instead of hiding. Sebastian records a new season's opening line: 'Some cases close you.' Beat: belonging earned, identity rewritten, the fog finally lifting.
